item.title: Housework
item.description: Words for jobs around the house and sharing them with your family or flatmates.

children.definition: to put things back in the right place so a room looks nice
children.example: Please tidy your room before the guests arrive.

children.definition: to wash the plates, cups and pots after a meal
children.example: I cook, and my brother does the washing-up.

children.definition: clothes and sheets that need washing or have just been washed
children.example: I do my laundry on Sunday evening.

children.definition: to make clothes smooth with a hot electric tool
children.example: He irons his shirt every morning before work.

children.definition: to clean the floor with an electric machine that sucks up dust
children.example: Can you vacuum the carpet in the living room?

children.definition: to clean the floor or yard with a brush
children.example: My grandmother sweeps the yard every morning.

children.definition: to clean the very small pieces of dirt off furniture with a cloth
children.example: I dust the shelves once a week.

children.definition: to put the sheets and blanket neatly on the bed after you get up
children.example: My mother always tells me to make the bed.

children.definition: to carry the bags of things you throw away out of the house
children.example: Whose turn is it to take out the rubbish?

children.definition: to give flowers and other plants water so they grow
children.example: Could you water the plants while I'm away?
The kitchen is really messy after the party.

children.definition: to divide jobs or things between two or more people
children.example: My flatmates and I share the housework.
